The objectives of this notebook will be to conduct a cluster analysis on each sample's BLM predictor variables to identify a typological classification of samples. This classification will be balled Typology2

This will be conducted under the baseline BLM assumptions (HA 10% Closed System) within the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet Clean version 2.

First, set the working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/calbert/Desktop/Trace-element-bioavailability-spatial-assessment/Zinc/5. Cluster analysis")
```

# Identifying Stream Typologies

Cluster analysis of all sites in WaDE Synoptic Survey except for pooled samples

Import dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("C:/Users/calbert/Desktop/Trace-element-bioavailability-spatial-assessment/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

head(dat)
```

Omit pooled samples from the analysis

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cluster_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(Flow_state != "Pooled")

str(cluster_dat$Flow_state)
```

## 1. Select variables

We'll use the scaled, log-transformed BLM predictors to conduct a PCA

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Variables to select
vars_to_select <- c("log_Temp_C", "pH", "log_DOC_uM",
                    "log_DIC_uM", "log_Cl_uM", "log_Ca_uM", 
                    "log_Mg_uM", "log_SO4_uM", "log_Na_uM", 
                    "log_K_uM", "log_Zn_uM", "log_Cu_uM")

# Scale these variables
scaled_blm_predict <- as.data.frame(
  scale(cluster_dat[vars_to_select])
)

# Peek
head(scaled_blm_predict)
```

## 2. K-means clustering

### i. Identifying the number of clusters

Run k-means using 2-5 and identify which number of clusters minimizes the overlap

```{r}
library(cluster)
library(dplyr)

# Silhouette check for k = 2:5
set.seed(123)

sil_df <- lapply(2:10, function(k) {
  
  km <- kmeans(
    scaled_blm_predict,
    centers = k,
    nstart = 50
  )
  
  sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(scaled_blm_predict))
  
  data.frame(
    k = k,
    mean_silhouette = mean(sil[, 3])
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

sil_df
```

### ii. Clustering (k=4)

```{r}
# Run k-means
set.seed(123)
kmeans_result4 <- kmeans(scaled_blm_predict, centers = 4, nstart = 50)

# Add cluster labels to your data
cluster_dat <- cluster_dat %>%
  mutate(cluster4 = as.factor(kmeans_result4$cluster))

# Check
str(cluster_dat$cluster4)
```

### iii. Clustering (k=3)

```{r}
# Run k-means
set.seed(123)
kmeans_result3 <- kmeans(scaled_blm_predict, centers = 3, nstart = 50)

# Add cluster labels to your data
cluster_dat <- cluster_dat %>%
  mutate(cluster3 = as.factor(kmeans_result3$cluster))

# Check
str(cluster_dat$cluster3)
```

## 4. Plot of clusters on PCA

### i. 4 clusters

```{r}
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Rename variables
scaled_blm_predict <- scaled_blm_predict %>%
  rename(
    Temp = log_Temp_C,
    DOC = log_DOC_uM,
    DIC = log_DIC_uM,
    `Cl-` = log_Cl_uM,
    Ca = log_Ca_uM,
    Mg = log_Mg_uM,
    `SO4 2-` = log_SO4_uM,
    Na = log_Na_uM,
    K = log_K_uM,
    Zn = log_Zn_uM,
    Cu = log_Cu_uM
  )

# Font sizes

title_size  <- 16
axis_title  <- 14
axis_text   <- 12
legend_title <- 14
legend_text  <- 12
strip_text   <- 12

#-------------------------------------------------
# 0) Force cluster order + set cluster colors
#-------------------------------------------------
cluster_colors <- c(
  "1" = "#D55E00",
  "2" = "#009E73",
  "3" = "#999999",
  "4" = "#56B4E9"
)

# Force correct ordering
cluster_for_plot <- cluster_dat$cluster4 %>%
  factor(levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4"))

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1) PCA
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_result <- prcomp(scaled_blm_predict, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_summary <- summary(pca_result)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2) PCA biplot (same depiction as your original)
#-------------------------------------------------
pca_cluster <- fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_result,
  geom.ind     = "point",
  col.var      = "black",
  habillage    = cluster_for_plot,
  addEllipses  = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Cluster",
  palette      = cluster_colors,
  repel        = TRUE 
) +
  labs(
    x = "PC1 (46.5%)",
    y = "PC2 (19.2%)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = axis_text) +
  theme(
    plot.title  = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = axis_title),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = axis_title),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = axis_text),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = axis_text),
    legend.title = element_text(size = legend_title),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = legend_text)
  )

# View
pca_cluster

# Define output directory
out_dir <- "Clustering by sample results"

# Create directory if it does not exist
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "PCA_Biplot_All_Sites_by_Cluster.png"),
  plot     = pca_cluster,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 5. Characterizing clusters

### i. Frequency table

4 clusters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# inherent characteristics 
site_char <- c("Type", "Regime", "Development")

cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(site_char), cluster4) %>%  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -cluster4,        
    names_to = "Variable",  
    values_to = "Value"     
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, cluster4, Value, name = "Freq") %>% 
  group_by(Variable, cluster4) %>%          
  mutate(RelFreq = prop.table(Freq) * 100)       

cluster_summary_table_pct
```

```{r}
)

```

### ii. Plot of relative frequencies

4 clusters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
# Combine variable and value
cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_summary_table_pct %>%
  mutate(Value_labeled = paste0(Variable, ": ", Value))

# Change the order of Variable Values
cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled <- factor(
  cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled,
  levels = c(
    "Type: Tributaries",
    "Type: Main Stem",
    
    "Development: Low",
    "Development: Medium",
    "Development: High",
    
    "Regime: NonPerennial",
    "Regime: Perennial"
  )
)

# Add cluster name as a variable for plotting purposes only
cluster_sizes <- cluster_dat %>%
  count(cluster4, name = "n_cluster")

cluster_summary_table_pct <- cluster_summary_table_pct %>%
  left_join(cluster_sizes, by = "cluster4") %>%
  mutate(
    cluster_name = paste0(
      "Cluster ", cluster4,
      " (n=", n_cluster, ")"
    )
  )

# Create a named color vector for all Value_labeled combinations
color_map <- c(
  "Type: Tributaries" = "#dadaeb",
  "Type: Main Stem" = "#756bb1",
  
  "Development: Low" = "#fdd49e",
  "Development: Medium" = "orange2",
  "Development: High" = "red3",
  
  "Regime: NonPerennial" = "lightblue",
  "Regime: Perennial" = "#1f78a4"
)

# Modify the legend to only display the categorical value
legend_labels <- gsub("^.*: ", "", levels(cluster_summary_table_pct$Value_labeled))

# Plot
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

rel_freq <- ggplot(
  cluster_summary_table_pct,
  aes(y = Variable, x = RelFreq, fill = Value_labeled)
) +
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = "fill",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster_name, ncol = 1, strip.position = "top") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Relative Frequency (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = axis_text) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x     = element_text(size = axis_title),
    axis.title.y     = element_text(size = axis_title),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = axis_text),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = axis_text),
    legend.title     = element_text(size = legend_title),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = legend_text),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      face = "bold",
      size = strip_text
    ),
    strip.placement  = "outside",
    panel.spacing    = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    legend.position  = "right",
    legend.box       = "vertical",
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = color_map,
    labels = legend_labels
    ) +
      theme(
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14
    )
      )
  

rel_freq

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Relative_freq_plots_by_cluster.png"),
  plot     = rel_freq,
  width    = 6,
  height   = 4,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

- Cluster 1: Highly developed perennial tributary sites

- Cluster 2: Non-perennial tributary sites

- Cluster 3: Mostly main stem sites

- Cluster 4: Perennial tributary sites

### iii. Rename clusters to typologies

And add pooled water as a typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cluster_dat <- cluster_dat %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster4)) %>%
  mutate(cluster = dplyr::recode(
    cluster,
    `1` = "Developed Perennial",
    `2` = "Non-Perennial",
    `3` = "Main Stem",
    `4` = "Perennial"
  )) %>%
  rename(Typology = cluster)

# Keep Sample_ID, cluster4, and Typology
typology_lookup <- cluster_dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, cluster4, Typology) %>%
  distinct()

# Join back to dat
dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cluster4 = factor(
      coalesce(as.character(cluster4), "Pooled"),
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "Pooled")
    ),
    Typology = if_else(is.na(Typology), "Pooled", Typology)
  )

# Quick check
unique(dat$Typology)

# Count samples in each Typology
dat %>%
  count(Typology)
```

Save cluster_name4 and Typology by 4 clusters columns to Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx and save in current working directory

```{r}
#-------------------------------------------
# 1. Read in file
#-------------------------------------------
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "C:/Users/calbert/Desktop/Trace-element-bioavailability-spatial-assessment/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx"

sheet_name <- "HA 10% Closed System"

ha10_dat <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name)

#-------------------------------------------
# 2. Build lookup table
#-------------------------------------------

typology_lookup <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Sample_ID,
    Typology,
    cluster4
  ) %>%
  distinct()

#-------------------------------------------
# 3. Remove pooled samples from the imported
#    Excel sheet and add Typology
#-------------------------------------------

ha10_dat_updated <- ha10_dat %>%
  semi_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

#-------------------------------------------
# 4. Checks
#-------------------------------------------

unique(ha10_dat_updated$Typology) # Ensure it exists
unique(ha10_dat_updated$Flow_state) # Should only be Flowing

#-------------------------------------------
# 5. Save updated workbook in working directory
#    by REPLACING the target sheet
#-------------------------------------------
library(writexl)

write_xlsx(
  list("HA 10% Closed System" = ha10_dat_updated),
  path = file.path(getwd(), "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx")
)
```

### c. Dominant typology for each site

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Count observations per Site × Typology
site_typology_counts <- dat %>%
  group_by(Network, Site, Typology) %>%
  summarise(n_obs = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Determine dominant Typology per Site
site_dominant <- site_typology_counts %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = n_obs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  rename(Dominant_Typology = Typology,
         Dominant_n = n_obs) %>%
  ungroup()

# Join back for full site-level table
site_summary_table <- site_typology_counts %>%
  left_join(site_dominant %>%
              dplyr::select(Network, Site, Dominant_Typology),
            by = c("Network", "Site")) %>%
  arrange(Network, Site, desc(n_obs))

# Merged table
nested_table <- site_summary_table %>%
  group_by(Network, Site) %>%
  summarise(
    Typologies_Observed = paste0(Typology, " (n=", n_obs, ")", collapse = "; "),
    Dominant_Typology   = first(Dominant_Typology),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Dominant_Typology = factor(Dominant_Typology)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Dominant_Typology, Network, Site)

nested_table

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  nested_table,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Sites_by_network_typology.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

### d. Relative frequency of clusters by site

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Create Actual_typology variable
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Actual_typology = case_when(
      
      # Main stem sites
      Type == "Main Stem" ~ "Main Stem Sites (n=106)",
      
      # Non-perennial tributaries
      Type == "Tributaries" &
        Regime == "NonPerennial" &
        Flow_state == "Flowing" ~ "Flowing Non-Perennial Tributary Sites (n=47)",
      
      # Pooled
      Type == "Tributaries" &
        Regime == "NonPerennial" &
        Flow_state == "Pooled" ~ "Pooled Non-Perennial Tributary Sites (n=30)",
      
      # Developed perennial tributaries
      Type == "Tributaries" &
        Regime == "Perennial" &
        Developed_lulc >= 80 ~ "Developed Perennial Tributary Sites (n=94)",
      
      # Perennial tributaries (<80% developed)
      Type == "Tributaries" &
        Regime == "Perennial" &
        Developed_lulc < 80 ~ "Perennial Tributary Sites (n=109)"
  )
  )

# Should be no missing
sum(is.na(dat$Actual_typology))

# Change order
dat$Actual_typology <- factor(dat$Actual_typology, levels = c(
  "Pooled Non-Perennial Tributary Sites (n=30)",
  "Flowing Non-Perennial Tributary Sites (n=47)",
  "Perennial Tributary Sites (n=109)",
  "Developed Perennial Tributary Sites (n=94)",
  "Main Stem Sites (n=106)"
))

# Check
str(dat$Actual_typology)

# Number of samples in each
summary(dat$Actual_typology)
```

Create a relative frequency plot of typology assignments by Actual_typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# 1. Summarize relative frequency of Typology within each site
cluster_freq_site <- dat %>%
  count(Actual_typology, Site, Typology, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(Actual_typology, Site) %>%
  mutate(relative_freq = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Assign cluster colors
typology_colors <- c(
  "Pooled" = "yellow3",
  "Non-Perennial" = "#009E73",
  "Perennial" = "#56B4E9",
  "Developed Perennial" = "#D55E00",
  "Main Stem" = "#999999"
  )

# 2. Plot horizontal stacked relative frequency bars
site_rel_freq <- ggplot(
  cluster_freq_site,
  aes(
    x = relative_freq,
    y = Site,
    fill = Typology
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +

  # Add sample counts within each bar segment
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ Actual_typology,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = typology_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Relative Frequency",
    y = "Site",
    fill = "Typology"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal"
  )

site_rel_freq

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Relative_freq_by_site.png"),
  plot     = site_rel_freq,
  width    = 12,
  height   = 10,
  dpi      = 300
)
```
